lyrics:
[Intro: lone piano figure, distant strings]

[Verse 1: female voice, hushed and pure]
How long have I been standing at this window with the light off?
I answer when I'm spoken to, I laugh on cue, I log off
Somewhere in the years I put myself away for keeping
Now I can't find where

[Pre-Chorus: strings swell, drums build]
I go through the day like a house with no one home

[Chorus: wall of guitars, male shouts answer each line]
(Shock me) Shock me back
(I can't feel it) I've been gone too long
(Shock me) Shock me back
Tell me something true and loud
Before I'm furniture
Before I'm stone
(Shock me back) Bring the weather in

[Verse 2: female voice, fuller, guitars held under]
Now that I can see how much of me was only waiting
I can't go back to quiet, I can't go back to fading
Open every window, turn the sirens and the rain up
I want all of it

[Pre-Chorus: strings swell, drums build]
I go through the day like a house with no one home

[Chorus: wall of guitars, male shouts answer each line]
(Shock me) Shock me back
(I can't feel it) I've been gone too long
(Shock me) Shock me back
Tell me something true and loud
Before I'm furniture
Before I'm stone
(Shock me back) Bring the weather in

[Bridge: male voice shouts and raps, female voice soars over it]
All this time I thought that I was resting
(I was rusting)
All this time I called it getting by
(I was hiding)
Nobody's coming with a key
So break it, break it, break it
Open

[Breakdown: piano and female voice alone]
Bring the weather in

[Final Chorus: heaviest, both voices, choir pad]
(Shock me) Shock me back
(I can't feel it) I've been gone too long
(Shock me) Shock me back
Tell me something true and loud
Before I'm furniture
Before I'm stone
(Shock me back) Bring the weather in

[Outro: piano figure, a window opening, rain]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 95 BPM, 4/4, E minor. Gothic and dramatic: fragile, then crushing.

VOICE: A female mezzo-soprano with a pure, classical, almost operatic tone, hushed in the verses and soaring with a strong vibrato in the choruses. A male voice shouts short lines in a rough, urgent rap-rock style, answering or doubling hers, and takes over the bridge.

INSTRUMENTS: A solitary piano figure. A string section. Thick, down-tuned distorted guitars playing slow, heavy chords. Deep bass. Powerful drums with a tight snare and double-kick bursts. A choir-like synth pad. Electronic pulses under the verses. Rain and a window as effects.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, piano and strings. 0:15 Verse 1. 0:45 Pre-chorus, one line over a build. 0:53 Chorus 1, the guitars and the male voice arrive together. 1:21 Verse 2. 1:51 Pre-chorus. 1:59 Chorus 2. 2:27 Bridge, the male voice leads and the female voice soars over him. 2:52 Breakdown, piano and one sung line. 3:00 Final chorus, heaviest. 3:28 Outro, the piano figure, a window opening, rain, ending at 3:45.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2000s gothic nu-metal: cinematic strings and piano against very dense guitars, the lead vocal clear and bright above everything.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The first shouted male line colliding with the first chorus at 0:53.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The numbness is specific to adult life: logging off, laughing on cue, getting by. The bridge refuses to wait for rescue, which the original, written at nineteen, did not yet know how to do.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Numb recognition, hunger, anger at wasted time, release.
